name: Clariden
description: Clariden is a selective dopaminergic modulator that suppresses the brain's default mode network, eliminating mind-wandering and intrusive thought for up to six hours. It creates a state of frictionless, tunnel-vision focus where extraneous sensory input is neurologically deprioritized. Widely prescribed to corporate analysts, surgical techs, and BCI-linked data workers.
effects: Total elimination of distraction and mind-wandering
Improved working memory retention during task
side_effects: Social blindness — inability to notice interpersonal cues
cultural_context: Clariden is the 'coffee of the corporate floor' — normalized to the point that refusing it in a high-pressure work environment draws suspicion. Tier 4 managers quietly pressure subordinates to take it before high-stakes presentations. On the Gray Zone, bootleg tablets called 'Glass' circulate, cut with stimulants that cause the scatter crash to hit harder.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 analyst realizes she's been on Clariden for 11 months straight and genuinely cannot remember the last time she had an unproductive thought — or a spontaneous one
A the Gray Zone kid gets hold of a bottle of genuine Clariden and uses it to study for a corporate placement exam, but the post-dose scatter crash hits during the test itself
A detective notes that the victim's autopsy showed Clariden in their system — meaning they would have been incapable of noticing someone following them
